title: clodcast sandbox - ship-tail probe
summary: A disposable episode whose only purpose is to exercise the web-only ship tail end to end against the real bucket, in a namespace no feed reads. Not a show; nothing links to it.
description_footer_text: Disposable test artifact from the clodcast sandbox. Not a published show.

segments.title: Intro
segments.text: This is the clodcast sandbox. It exists to prove one thing: that the ship tail works end to end against a real bucket, without touching a real feed. Everything here was produced by the same renderer the live shows use, on the same house voice, with the same intro music.

segments.title: What is under test
segments.text: The interesting part is not the audio. It is the four steps after the audio: putting the mp3 and the cover into object storage, upserting an entry into a feed manifest, firing the site's deploy hook, and writing the dedup log. Those four are the only part of the pipeline a local dry run cannot rehearse, because a dry run deliberately stops before them.

segments.title: How isolation works
segments.text: Four keys do the work. A key prefix namespaces the audio and the cover, so a sandbox episode published on the same day as a real one cannot overwrite it. A manifest name puts the feed entry in its own object. A slug prefix keeps the permalink and the feed identifier out of every real show. And every segment carries a null source, so the shared dedup log gains nothing and no real story is ever marked as covered by a test.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.text: If you are hearing this from a public URL, the ship tail works. This episode is disposable and can be deleted from the bucket at any time without consequence. Thanks for listening to a test.
